What Is a Commercial Rooftop Unit

A Commercial Rooftop Unit is a self contained HVAC system placed on a curb on your roof. Inside that cabinet you will find the supply fan return fan cooling section heating section filters control board and often an economizer for free cooling. The unit connects to your duct system through a roof curb and sends conditioned air through the building. Learn more about the concept on this rooftop unit overview.

Why do so many San Diego buildings use rooftop units

  • They save indoor space for people and products
  • Service techs can access the unit without walking through your business
  • Units are modular so upgrades and swaps are faster
  • Economizers let you use cool coastal air in spring and fall which helps cut power costs

Why San Diego Buildings Rely On RTUs

San Diego has microclimates. A shop in La Jolla fights salt air. A warehouse in Otay Mesa deals with dusty winds. A gym in Pacific Beach sees heavy use and sweat load after 5 p.m. A medical office in Kearny Mesa needs steady temperature low noise and clean air. A proper Commercial Rooftop Unit setup answers all of that.

  • Marine layer mornings and sunny afternoons demand smart controls that adjust quickly
  • Coastal zones need coil coatings and hardware that resist corrosion
  • Inland areas get hotter in summer so variable speed fans and higher cooling capacity matter
  • Many cities in the county follow Title 24 energy rules so economizers demand control ventilation and better fan control help meet code and lower bills

New Installation and Replacement

Planning a new Commercial Rooftop Unit in San Diego or replacing an old one We start with your building not just a box on a spec sheet. A unit that is too big short cycles and wastes energy. A unit that is too small runs nonstop and still misses the setpoint. We run a load and site inspection look at your ducts and review your business hours and occupancy.

1 Site visit and assessment

  • Measure roof curb and duct connections
  • Check structural needs
  • Review electrical service and gas lines if needed
  • Look at outside air intake placement to avoid kitchen hoods or auto exhaust

2 System selection

  • Cooling and heating capacity that matches your space and use
  • Single zone or multi zone need
  • Economizer choice for free cooling on cool days
  • Filter options for dust pollen and smoke days
  • Variable speed fans for lower power use and quieter operation

3 Permits and planning

  • We handle permit paperwork with the City of San Diego or your local city
  • We schedule crane lifts traffic control if needed and coordinate with your property manager

4 Swap day

  • Protect indoor areas before work starts
  • Disconnect and remove the old unit
  • Set the new unit with a crane and secure to the curb
  • Connect power gas if present controls and ducts
  • Commission the system with full checks and diagnostics

5 Tuning and turnover

  • Balance airflow to help even out hot and cold spots
  • Program schedules and setpoints
  • Train your staff on basic use and filter checks
  • Schedule the first maintenance visit

We service most brands and carry parts that fit common units found on San Diego roofs. From 3 ton light commercial units to larger multi fan cabinets we install what fits the job the roof and your budget.

Preventive Maintenance Plans

Seasonal timing that works well in San Diego

Air Quality Duct Cleaning and Energy Savings

Sky Clean Air started with duct cleaning sealing and indoor air quality and that gives your rooftop system a real boost. Why Because a rooftop unit can only push clean air if the ducts are clean and sealed.

How we improve air and efficiency

Cleaner ducts and coils reduce static pressure. That means the fan uses less power runs quieter and reaches setpoint faster. Staff and tenants notice the difference right away. Consider airflow balancing for added comfort.

Signs Your Unit Needs Service

Catching issues early saves money and avoids big repairs. Do any of these sound familiar

  • Uneven temperatures across suites or rooms
  • Rising energy bills without a change in use
  • AC runs nonstop or cycles off and on quickly
  • Water on the roof by the unit
  • Ice on lines or coils
  • Musty smells or visible dust at supply grilles
  • Staff complaints about stuffy rooms
  • Thermostat loses its schedule or shows error codes
  • Loud or new noises from the roof

If you said yes to any of these a quick diagnostic check can point the way. Call {{phone}} and we will check it out.

Many sites see lower demand charges with smarter fan control and proper staging. Want us to review your setup and share quick wins We are happy to help.

Special Considerations in San Diego

Our city and county throw a few curveballs at rooftop units. We plan for those from day one.

Coastal corrosion

Salt air attacks coils and fasteners. We use coated coils sealed electrical boxes and stainless hardware on coastal sites. We also suggest rinse visits during peak salt season which can be part of AC maintenance.

Marine layer and economizers

Cool mornings are perfect for free cooling. We tune outdoor air sensors so you use the breeze without bringing in foggy damp air that can cause sticky rooms.

Wildfire smoke days

We set filters and outside air controls to protect indoor air quality. This can include temporary changes to outside air intake and filter ratings with a plan to return to normal once air clears.

Rooftop access and cranes

Downtown Mission Valley or UTC can be busy. We handle crane permits flagging and timing so neighbors and tenants stay happy.

Solar arrays

We work around solar panels and coordinate with your solar provider when needed so wires and arrays remain safe.

Older buildings

We often find old curbs and duct transitions. Curb adapters and smart sheet metal work keep projects on track without rebuilding the entire roof opening.

How Clean Ducts Protect Your Investment

You would not install a new engine and leave a clogged exhaust. The same goes for a rooftop unit and ducts. Dirty ducts raise static pressure. The fan works harder energy use climbs and rooms still feel stuffy. Our duct services help your new or existing unit shine

  • Camera inspection to find buildup and leaks
  • Cleaning supply and return trunks and branches
  • Sealing connections especially at the roof curb
  • Adding insulation to exposed ducts on roofs if needed
  • Verifying airflow at diffusers for comfort with duct balancing

Cleaner ducts also help reduce allergies from dust and pollen. That is a win for staff comfort and productivity.

The Value of Proper Sizing and Airflow

Bigger is not better. Correct sizing and clean ducts keep comfort steady and costs down. A unit that is too big may cool fast but leave humidity high and rooms clammy. A unit that is too small will never catch up on hot afternoons. Good airflow is just as important. Kinks crushed flex runs or leaky joints all hurt performance. We measure and fix those details so the box on the roof can do its job. Consider a thorough HVAC inspection and duct balancing.

Recent Blogs
faqs: What is a commercial rooftop unit?
A commercial rooftop unit is a type of heating and cooling system installed on the roof of a commercial building to control indoor temperature and air quality.
How do I know if my business needs a rooftop unit?
If your business requires consistent indoor comfort and efficient temperature control, a rooftop unit may be a good option.
What types of buildings can use rooftop units?
Rooftop units are commonly used in office buildings, retail stores, restaurants, warehouses, and schools.
How often should a rooftop unit be serviced?
Regular maintenance, typically at least twice a year, is recommended to keep your unit running smoothly.
What are the benefits of installing a rooftop unit?
Rooftop units save indoor space, can be easily accessed for maintenance, and help improve air circulation and comfort.
Can Sky Clean Air help with rooftop unit installation?
Yes, Sky Clean Air provides professional installation and service for commercial rooftop units.
How long does a rooftop unit typically last?
With proper maintenance, a rooftop unit can serve your building for many years.
What maintenance does a rooftop unit require?
Regular filter changes, cleaning, and inspection of components help ensure the unit works efficiently.
Does Sky Clean Air repair existing rooftop units?
Yes, Sky Clean Air offers repair services for commercial rooftop units.
How can I get a quote for rooftop unit services?
You can contact Sky Clean Air directly to schedule an evaluation and receive a personalized quote.
